page: Amazon Web Services r8gn.medium is a memory-optimized virtual machine instance powered by the AWS Nitro hypervisor. It features a single dedicated ARMv9-based AWS Graviton Neoverse-V2 physical core operating at 2.8 GHz. The processor includes 64 KB of L1d cache, 2 MB of L2 cache, and 36 MB of L3 cache, with hardware-accelerated AES cryptography support. The instance is configured with 8.0 GB of system memory, yielding an 8.0 GB per core ratio. It does not include local storage or integrated GPUs, and it provides a baseline network bandwidth of 3 Gbps.

In benchmark evaluations, the single-core architecture of the r8gn.medium delivers average performance in single-threaded tasks, such as stress-ng CPU tests, Geekbench single-core workloads, and gzip compression. It demonstrates strong single-threaded performance in bzip3 decompression. However, because the instance is limited to a single vCPU, its multi-core performance in Geekbench and stress-ng is poor. Memory bandwidth tests show weak to poor throughput, with uncached large-block reads at 30.32 GB/sec and writes at 11.59 GB/sec. Database operations, Redis SET performance, and static web serving throughput also fall into weak or poor categories due to the single-core constraint.

From a cost-efficiency perspective, the r8gn.medium offers a high memory-to-vCPU ratio for entry-level ARM64 workloads without the overhead of multi-core licensing or excess compute capacity. It is best suited for lightweight, memory-intensive applications that do not require parallel processing, such as small-scale caching, single-threaded data processing, lightweight database operations, and basic text processing tasks.
